swap.evidence: Swapped into (a) a bike-share depot's reservation flow and (b) a school's AV-equipment loan desk. Surviving unchanged: wrench-glyph-plus-name header in bold body sans; grey-green ground with white bordered cards; identical pale-green icon tiles on every card; green availability pills; generic month grid with 'Open' tags; half-width dl-summary confirm page. Bound to this product: only copy (tool names, deposits, Saturday/Wednesday sessions, 14 Mill Lane, the desk phone, 'returned when it comes back clean and working'). With the name and copy hidden, a reader could not tell it is a volunteer tool library.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community/volunteer booking flow: near-white ground, one green or teal accent, system-feeling sans, bordered list cards with thumbnail, pill status badges, single-column public-service forms with error summary. Predicted opposite: a warm, hand-made 'community noticeboard' look with kraft paper, stamps and handwritten type. The render matches the default on every identity-carrying element (accent green #1f5a3a, Avenir-like sans, thumbnail cards, pills, error summary pattern). The one recorded tie to the product's world, 'the green of the library's membership card', is invisible to a visitor because no card, tag or object carrying it appears.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online reservation for a community toy library run from a church hall, collect at opening hours, deposit in person'. Predicted choices: grey/white ground, a single green accent, uniform cards with a placeholder icon, availability badges, a calendar marking open days, a basket with session radios, a confirm form, a confirmation summary. Overlap is near-total; the only element shaped by this brief (session days marked 'Open' in the pick-up calendar) is also what that brief would produce.

findings.title: Identical placeholder icon tiles stand in for every tool's picture
findings.description: Each of the ten tool cards shows the same 96px pale-green square with the same wrench glyph, whether the tool is a ladder, a hedge trimmer or a wallpaper steamer. The tile looks like an unfilled image slot.
findings.impact: Members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' get no visual cue to tell tools apart, and the repeated stand-in is likely to make the page read as unfinished, which may lower trust that a reservation will actually be honoured.
findings.recommendation: Decide what each card's visual slot is for: a real photo of the library's own item, a tool-specific mark, or nothing. If it stays, it must differ per tool; if not, remove it rather than show a stand-in.

findings.title: No identity floor or signature: name in body text over a category-default frame
findings.description: Across all routes the only identity is 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body sans beside a stock wrench glyph. The membership-card green the design is said to come from is not tied to any visible object, and nothing from the library's world (the room, the desk, tool tags, the session list) appears. All three specificity tests fail.
findings.impact: Members, many older and reserving a few times a year, may not recognise this as their library's own service rather than a third-party booking tool, weakening the 'neighbourly' attribute the brief asks for.
findings.recommendation: Decide one signature that only this library has, taken from its own mechanism (for example how sessions or the desk work), and set the name as a designed mark carrying the declared membership-card green; keep controls conventional.

findings.title: Tool names truncated with an ellipsis on phones, making two drills indistinguishable
findings.description: At 375 px card titles are clipped to one line: both cordless drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', the ladder 'Extension ladder 3 m ...'. The distinguishing detail (one vs two batteries, length) is exactly what is cut.
findings.impact: On the primary device, members may open the wrong drill or must open each card to compare, against the brief's 'the drill with two batteries' wording.
findings.recommendation: Decide that tool names wrap in full at every width; the card layout must absorb two or three lines.

findings.title: Search field drops below the full tool list on phones
findings.description: At 375 px the 'Search tools' label, input, Search button and filter button sit after all ten cards, near the bottom of a ~2600 px page, whereas at 1280 they precede the list.
findings.impact: On the primary device members with a tool in mind may not find search until they have scrolled the whole list; the order also differs between phone and desktop.
findings.recommendation: Decide one reading order for find that puts the search before the list at every width.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar overlaps the calendar and its button sits outside the content column
findings.description: On the tool page the full-width white action bar cuts across the calendar rows (week of 11-17 hidden), and the 'Reserve this tool' button is flush to the window edge (right edge x 1264) instead of aligning with the 1184 content edge. In the added state the toast also sits over the weekday header.
findings.impact: The session days members need to pick may be hidden under the bar, and the misaligned button looks detached from the page, which may make the main action read as an overlay rather than part of the form. Partly a full-page-capture artefact; the alignment issue is not.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the bottom bar is needed at desktop widths; where it stays, align its contents to the content column and reserve space so it never covers the calendar.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions laid out unevenly and ordered latest-first
findings.description: At 1280 the six session radios render as one full-width row (Wed 28 Oct) followed by five narrow cards whose labels wrap over three lines. Sessions run from latest to earliest and include 10 and 14 Oct, before the chosen pick-up day of Saturday 17 October.
findings.impact: Reading dates against their natural order and wrapped over three lines is likely to slow the core 'choose the session' task and may lead members to choose a session before their tool is collectable.
findings.recommendation: Decide a single, chronological layout for session choices in which each date reads on one line.

findings.title: Pages end in an unfilled grey band at wide widths
findings.description: On basket, confirm and done at 1280 the white footer strip ends mid-viewport and the page ground continues as a flat grey band beneath it (basket y 807-900, done y 700-900). Confirm and done content also occupies only the left half of the column.
findings.impact: A footer that stops short reads as unfinished on desktop, undercutting 'careful'.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages end: the footer should meet the viewport bottom or the ground should be continuous.

findings.title: Done page gives the reservation no confirming moment and keeps 'Basket (1)'
findings.description: The done page sets reservation number FT-4471 at body size in a grey-label table and the masthead still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is made.
findings.impact: The member's job on done is to know the reservation is made and what to bring; the stale basket count may suggest the tool is still only held, and the number the desk may ask for is not easy to find again.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the member must carry away (session, number, deposit) and give that the page's weight; clear held state once confirmed.

findings.title: No-results search state looks identical to the default list
findings.description: With 'sewing machine' in the search field the page shows all ten tools unchanged and no message that nothing matched.
findings.impact: Members may believe the listed tools match their search, or that search failed silently. (May be a capture of a state that was not triggered; flag for verification.)

evidence.detail: query present, full list shown, no empty-state message

findings.recommendation: Decide what an unmatched search shows, in the desk volunteer's voice, and make sure the captured state actually exercises it.

strengths: Copy in the desk volunteer's voice: concrete, brief, no exclamation marks ('returned when it comes back clean and working', 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower').
One filled primary per page, conventional controls and a well-formed error summary: correct for Operate surfaces.
Dark theme is composed (lighter greens, lighter cards on darker ground), matching the evening phone use scene.
keep: Keep the volunteer voice and the one-primary-per-page discipline; add identity without adding loud moves.
